map.title: [Wayfinder Map] Decoupled Minutes & Event Architecture with Decomposed Event Challenger
map.body:
## Destination

Decouple minutes and event-rate modeling into independent modules ($M_{\text{mins}}$ and $M_{\text{events}}$) with dedicated validation gates (Tier 1 Minutes Gate, Tier 2 Oracle Event Gate, Tier 3 Integrated Gate), and evaluate `DecomposedEventChallengerModel` as the first candidate event rate engine. Complete when architectural interfaces, backtesting harnesses, and candidate implementation are locked into reviewable decisions and ready for execution.

## Notes

Domain: FPL score projection math, statistical backtesting, and model architecture.
Consult Wayfinder, antislop, domain-modeling, and grilling.
P1/P2/P3 denote priority/impact triage.
Open children are decision questions, not automatically approved changes.
Reference evidence and proposals stored in `docs/research/decoupled-projection-architecture/`.

## Decisions so far

<!-- the index: one line per closed ticket, enough to judge relevance, then zoom the link for the detail the ticket holds -->

- [[P1] How should BaseMinutesModel, BaseEventRateModel, and CompositeProjectionModel be structured?](https://github.com/JubileeZ/fpl-jubilee-ascent/issues/160): MinutesPrediction dataclass, BaseMinutesModel, BaseEventRateModel, and CompositeProjectionModel with dynamic composite spec resolution and Oracle minutes bypass.
- [[P1] How should Oracle Minutes injection and Tier 2 Event Gate be wired into walkforward backtests?](https://github.com/JubileeZ/fpl-jubilee-ascent/issues/161): Triple join on (player_id, gameweek_id, fixture_id), blended points target, Formation XI delta > 0 with block bootstrap P >= 0.60, playable pool relative bias tolerance (+0.02), and captaincy regret guardrail (+0.15 pts/GW).
- [[P2] How should the standalone Tier 1 Minutes Gate CLI and evaluation metrics operate?](https://github.com/JubileeZ/fpl-jubilee-ascent/issues/162): commands/evaluate_minutes CLI with active pool MAE/RMSE primary, 3-way participation Brier score, 60+ min starter discrimination (ROC-AUC, Recall, Precision), and Tier 1 gate requiring Δ_MAE > 0, bootstrap P >= 0.60, Brier non-regression (+0.002), and starter recall tolerance (-0.005).
- [[P1] How should Open-Play vs. Set-Piece xG decomposition and Aerial Target Prior be regularized?](https://github.com/JubileeZ/fpl-jubilee-ascent/issues/163): Rejected: FPL data lacks Opta shot-type tags; synthetic OP/SP splits ruled out of scope to avoid ungrounded optimizer traps. Retain Champion unified xG shrinkage (K=2400 DEF, K=360 ATK).

## Not yet specified

- Specialized minutes model $M_{\text{mins}}$ (manager rotation entropy, rest-interval fatigue decay, and continuous substitution hazard curves)
- Live operational pipeline integration for weekly dashboard and transfer solve scenarios

## Out of scope

- Production deployment of unvalidated models
- Breaking existing BaseModel or CLI solver contracts
- Banned dead levers from Candidate Ledger (club 11-man mass conservation, in-season ridge G/A refits, unseeded defender K relaxation, raw Poisson multipliers)
- Synthetic OP/SP xG decomposition without primary Opta event-stream data (Issue #163)

tickets.title: [P1] How should BaseMinutesModel, BaseEventRateModel, and CompositeProjectionModel be structured?
tickets.body:
## Question

How should the base interfaces (`BaseMinutesModel`, `BaseEventRateModel`, `CompositeProjectionModel`) be structured in `models/base.py` and `models/__init__.py` to decouple participation duration from per-minute event rates while preserving 100% backward compatibility for existing monoliths (`def_xg_shrink_challenger`, `learned_start_challenger`)?

## Observed evidence & proposal

Currently, `BaseModel.predict()` couples minutes and rates inside one monolithic pass. The proposed refactor introduces:
1. `MinutesPrediction` dataclass containing `p_dnp`, `p_start`, `p_sub_in`, `xmins_if_start`, `xmins_if_sub_in`, `projected_minutes`, and `p_60_plus`.
2. `BaseMinutesModel` with `predict_minutes()` and `predict_states()`.
3. `BaseEventRateModel` with `predict_rates(df_feat, minutes_pred, horizon)`.
4. `CompositeProjectionModel(BaseModel)` that delegates to any minutes and event model pair, with deterministic overrides when `external_xmins` is present.
5. Dynamic model spec resolution `composite:<minutes_key>:<event_key>` in `models.get_model()`.

## Decision acceptance

1. `CompositeProjectionModel` satisfies `assert_projection_contract` on all 13 additive components.
2. Legacy models continue to inherit and execute `BaseModel.predict` unchanged.
3. Model resolution `composite:learned_start:def_xg_shrink` instantiates and predicts without error.
4. Ruff clean, all existing unit tests pass.

tickets.title: [P1] How should Oracle Minutes injection and Tier 2 Event Gate be wired into walkforward backtests?
tickets.body:
## Question

How should the walk-forward backtest runner in `backtesting/walkforward.py` and promotion gate in `backtesting/promotion.py` isolate per-minute event accuracy using actual match minutes, and what decision bounds define a Tier 2 pass?

## Observed evidence & proposal

In the October 2026 diagnostic (`docs/research/multi-component-ladder/multi-component-ladder.md`), conditioning on actual minutes dropped playable pool bias from -1.11 to -0.08 pts and increased correlation by +52%.
Proposed implementation:
1. Add `oracle_minutes: bool = False` to `WalkforwardConfig`.
2. Add `_inject_oracle_minutes()` joining `df_perf` actual match minutes into `df_feat["external_xmins"]` at `(player_id, gameweek_id, fixture_id)` granularity.
3. Compute `oracle_formation_xi_regret` when `oracle_minutes=True`.
4. Implement `evaluate_oracle_event_gate()` in `backtesting/promotion.py`: requires $\Delta_{\text{oracle}} > 0$, block bootstrap $P \ge 0.60$, and signed bias bounded within $\pm 0.10$ pts.

## Decision acceptance

1. Running walkforward backtest with `oracle_minutes=True` executes without data leakage.
2. `evaluate_oracle_event_gate()` correctly issues pass/fail verdicts on Oracle Formation Regret and bias tolerance.
3. Standard walkforward backtest (`oracle_minutes=False`) runs identically to master.

tickets.title: [P2] How should the standalone Tier 1 Minutes Gate CLI and evaluation metrics operate?
tickets.body:
## Question

What CLI interface and statistical metrics should evaluate standalone Minutes Projection Models ($M_{\text{mins}}$) against ground truth, and what thresholds govern the Tier 1 Minutes Gate?

## Observed evidence & proposal

Currently, minutes errors are evaluated only as a secondary guardrail (`xmins_mae <= champ * 1.01`) during full-season point backtests. A dedicated standalone evaluator is needed to test rotation models independently.
Proposed implementation:
1. Create `commands/evaluate_minutes.py` (`python -m commands.evaluate_minutes --model ... --champion ... --data-dir ...`).
2. Primary metrics: Minutes MAE and RMSE on active players.
3. Multiclass participation Brier score across `(p_dnp, p_start, p_sub_in)`.
4. Starter discrimination: ROC-AUC, Precision, and Recall on capturing 60+ minute appearances.
5. `evaluate_minutes_gate()`: Requires positive MAE delta, non-regressing Brier score, recall tolerance within $-0.005$, and circular block bootstrap $P \ge 0.60$.

## Decision acceptance

1. CLI produces structured JSON metrics and comparative gate verdicts against Champion minutes.
2. Brier score correctly handles 3-way participation states.
3. Unit tests in `tests/test_decoupled_models.py` verify gate behavior on synthetic fixtures.

tickets.title: [P1] How should Open-Play vs. Set-Piece xG decomposition and Aerial Target Prior be regularized?
tickets.body:
## Question

How should non-penalty expected goals be split into Open-Play ($xG_{\text{OP}}$) and Set-Piece ($xG_{\text{SP}}$) channels in `DecomposedEventChallengerModel`, and how do we prevent set-piece noise from violating the Candidate Ledger ban on unseeded defender relaxation?

## Observed evidence & proposal

The Champion (`def_xg_shrink_challenger`) shrinks all defender $xG$ uniformly at $K=2400$, under-projecting offensive fullbacks and dominant aerial center-backs.
Proposed mechanism:
1. Decompose historical $xG$ into $xG_{\text{OP}}$ and $xG_{\text{SP}}$ using threat/creativity ratios or explicit tags.
2. Shrink $xG_{\text{OP}}$ with $K_{\text{DEF, OP}} = 1200$, $K_{\text{ATK, OP}} = 360$.
3. Gate defender set-piece shrinkage $K_{\text{DEF, SP}} \in [900, 2400]$ via an **Aerial Target Prior** $\tau_i$ ($K_{\tau} = 1800$), enforcing a hard floor of $K \ge 900$ to avoid the optimizer's curse.
4. Scale modalities by damped opponent concession multipliers ($\psi_{\text{opp}, \text{OP}}, \psi_{\text{opp}, \text{SP}}$), shrunk by $s_{\text{mod}} = 0.35$ and hard-clipped to $[0.75, 1.30]$.

## Decision acceptance

1. Gated shrinkage floor ($K \ge 900$) strictly prevents volatile defender spikes.
2. Modality concession multipliers are mean-normalized so overall league bias remains zero-sum.
3. No club-level DEF priors are stacked (respecting the Dead Lever ban).

tickets.title: [P2] How should LOO Teammate Finishing Multiplier and Shot-Volume GK Saves be calibrated?
tickets.body:
## Question

How should teammate finishing skill modulate the Ridge Poisson assist GLM without overfitting, and how should opponent shot volume and shot danger calibrate goalkeeper saves?

## Observed evidence & proposal

In-season Ridge G/A refits previously failed promotion due to chasing noisy assist hauls. Conversely, pure $xA$ ignores that passes to elite finishers (Haaland) convert at higher rates.
Proposed mechanism:
1. Retain the stable Ridge Poisson $xA$ GLM ($\lambda = 10.0$).
2. Modulate assist rates by a leave-one-out (LOO) club finishing multiplier:
   $$\Phi_{\text{club}(-i)} = \text{clip}\left(1 + \frac{\sum_{j \ne i} \omega_j (G_j - xG_j)}{\sum_{j \ne i} \omega_j xG_j + 25.0}, 0.88, 1.15\right)$$
3. Goalkeeper save intensity $\hat{r}_{\text{saves}} = \hat{s}_{i, 0} \cdot \text{clip}(V_{\text{opp}}^{0.45} \cdot D_{\text{opp}}^{-0.25}, 0.70, 1.45)$, where $V_{\text{opp}}$ is opponent shot volume (threat) and $D_{\text{opp}}$ is shot danger ($xG/\text{threat}$).

## Decision acceptance

1. Assist conversion multiplier is strictly leave-one-out and centered across the gameweek pool.
2. Goalkeeper save adjustments correctly reward keepers facing perimeter-shooting teams while capping downside.
3. Playable pool signed bias remains within $[-0.10, +0.10]$.

tickets.title: [P2] What test fixtures and verification suite prove bit-for-bit backward compatibility?
tickets.body:
## Question

What test fixtures, integration assertions, and gate checks prove that decoupling minutes from event rates introduces zero regressions to legacy champions and existing dashboard/solve commands?

## Observed evidence & proposal

Proposed test plan:
1. Unit tests in `tests/test_decoupled_models.py` verifying:
   - `CompositeProjectionModel` satisfies `ProjectionContract`.
   - `states_from_external_minutes` produces deterministic participation states.
   - Standalone minutes metrics calculation and gate verdict.
   - `evaluate_oracle_event_gate` pass/fail evaluation.
2. Bit-for-bit parity check between `CompositeProjectionModel(learned_start, def_xg_shrink)` and native `def_xg_shrink_challenger`.
3. Validation commands:
   - `uv run ruff check .`
   - `uv run pytest tests/test_decoupled_models.py -q`
   - `uv run pytest tests/ -k "def_xg_shrink_challenger or learned_start_challenger or solve or dashboard" -q`
   - `bash tests/verify.sh`

## Decision acceptance

1. All new tests pass cleanly.
2. Existing 547+ suite tests pass with 0 regressions.
3. Delivery gate `bash tests/verify.sh` passes.
